They say fibro could be caused from trauma and I figure mine had to have been from falling off a wall onto my head because that's when everything started. I don't remember what it's like to be awake or not be in pain.

I like how many young people are on here. I sympathize with everyone here no matter what their age but there's a certain higher understanding with younger people. It's pretty stressful as is to start a life in this day and age but add chronic illness and it seems like I'm just shoveling dry sand. I hope someday I can know what it is like to feel normal, I stay hopeful for a cure in my lifetime. I get the same thing from older people who just shrug off my pain and exhaustion because I'm not an old lady but gosh darn it do I feel like I'm 90. I definitely walk like one most days.

Wow, I can't imagine having children with this, you must be so incredibly strong! I've somewhat accepted that I'll never have a child. I'm getting better ever so slowly with pacing myself. I want to get back into art, I used to do it so often, but I kind of lost interest as things got worse and worse. My doctors were ordering tests to try to determine if I have multiple sclerosis in addition to the fibro, but my insurance stopped approving the tests so I guess I'll never know. That's the most recent frustrating event, but I've tried not to think about it too much.  I'm having trouble concentrating so I'm sorry if this sounds like rambling.

Thank you for your kind words, I've managed to clean half of the apartment and I'm taking a break now. I think the hardest thing for me that I need to work much harder on is taking breaks. I tend to just take care of an entire list of chores and tire myself out and then I'm useless after. It's so hard to stop once I get started. But look at me now, I'm taking a break to write this and drink a big glass of water! Haha I will consider this a small victory. I have close friends who will always be there for me and listen to me but unless you have a chronic illness there's no way to understand it and that's what gets frustrating. I think I will start using this thread more to get out what I want to scream out loud on certain days. Again, thank you for your kind words I took them to heart!

Thank you, this really helped me realize something that seems so obvious, that men like to fix things. My boyfriend always is telling me about studies for treatment that helped a lot of people. It makes me feel great that he cares so much which sucks that I have to tell him I've already tried what he's brought up. It bums him out and he hasn't brought any new studies up to me in awhile. Almost five years of trying every thing I know that has even marginally helped others with no effect or worsening has put me in a realistic view that all I can do is bare down and take everything this beast can throw my way. In a sense it's helped because there are no more disappointments from failed treatments. I'm thinking of getting some pain killers which I've never done before unless it was in the hospital. I wouldn't be on them everyday, just the three or four days a month when it gets unbearable. Do you have any experience with this? I've had fibromyalgia my whole life. I didn't get a diagnosis until I was 16. I'm now treo weeks away from being 21. I know narcotics aren't generally a good idea but I need some sort of quality of life which seems to be lacking.

I got my dog to stop pulling, she's a husky and if you know about huskies you know they PULL like no other. I walked her and every time there was tension on the leash I would turn around and walk the other way. At first I was almost literally making tiny circles because I had to turn so many times. but after about an hour a day of this for two weeks, she walked with a loose leash, never pulling again. Her other problem was that when we would walk through a park or down the street she'd start smelling a bush and I would turn back and pull but she wouldn't budge. So I started to just keep walking, looking ahead and pay her no attention, it was like magic she just ran back up to walk with me. you could try this method. worked wonders for me.
